title: Say where, when and how
objective: Choose a preposition that shows the relationship you mean.

slides.title: Ask a simple question
body: Where? The leaf was on the table. When? We wrote during class.
How? We looked at the leaf with a hand lens. With introduces the tool.

slides.title: Follow a field note
body: “At noon, we saw a frog on a rock. We looked at the frog with binoculars.”
At gives a time, on gives a surface and with gives a tool.
Change the setting to a pond. Which word would show that the frog was in the water?

slides.title: Read the first case together
body: Field note: The leaf was ___ the table. We looked at it ___ a hand lens. We wrote notes ___ the visit.

slides.title: Try it with a partner
body: Choose a word that shows the item rested on the surface. Write the sentence.
Choose a word that introduces the tool.
Think about where the item was.

slides.title: Try a new case
body: Field note: The shell was ___ the desk. We looked at it ___ a hand lens. We wrote notes ___ the visit.

slides.title: Work on your own
body: Choose a word that shows the item rested on the surface. Write the sentence.
Choose a word that introduces the tool.
Complete the last sentence to show that notes were written while the visit was happening.

slides.title: Test a new sentence
body: Write a short field note. Have your partner point to a phrase for place, time or tool and explain its job.
